cohort: 171 maternal mortality cases and 523 alive mothers matched for year of delivery, mother's age at delivery, and city of residence in Isfahan, Iran
finding: Being an immigrant, having a history of proximate medical cause, vaginal delivery, and illiteracy were associated with increased odds of maternal mortality, while using public antenatal care and planned pregnancy had a protective effect.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with a 2.28 times higher odds of maternal mortality compared to cesarean delivery.
